reasoning: The task examples disambiguate the flattened exponent notation: t=0 moves one position and t=1 moves two, so legal jump lengths are powers of two. Tokens move independently and the minimum moves for a token at i to leave prefix k equal the minimum popcount of a displacement in [k+1-i,n-i]. Among displacements at most n-i, the farthest reachable with at most s jumps is the sum of its s highest set bits: repeated powers can be combined without increasing jump count. Thus the required move count increases by one at i and at each partial sum of descending set bits, except the final endpoint n. Add the token multiplicity at these thresholds and prefix-sum to obtain all answers in O(n log n), using unbounded integers.
